competitions.title: Cash Rush Competition
competitions.field_context: Campus startup simulation competing under strict 120-minute time constraint with ₹300 seed capital.

service_breakdown.name: Dynamic web curiosity funnel
service_breakdown.mechanism: Web experience ending with QR code redirecting to LinkedIn as a curiosity hook

service_breakdown.name: Campus quiz challenge
service_breakdown.mechanism: Winners got paid, losers paid the squad

deliverables: Live campus crowd quiz mechanics & execution
Team engine: live caricature keepsake sketches (team deliverable)

story.setup: Teams got ₹300 and 120 minutes to grow it on campus however they could.
story.key_decision: We sold experiences, not goods: designed a curiosity-monetization thesis pairing a web funnel to LinkedIn with a live campus crowd quiz, alongside on-the-spot caricature keepsakes from our squad. Total costs were ₹45 (paper and marker).
story.result: Services brought in ₹2,400 (₹1,050 web funnel, ₹550 quiz, ₹800 caricatures). The fund ended at ₹2,655: 1st place and the ₹7,000 prize.
story.takeaway: Sell what costs nothing to produce. With 120 minutes on the clock, experiences beat inventory.

proof.alt: Ashoka Cash Rush Championship Team celebrating
proof.caption: Cash Rush Championship Team · Ashoka University

competitions.title: Advertising & Brand Pitch
competitions.field_context: Offline university brand pitch sprint representing Rishihood University.

story.setup: Represented Rishihood University offline at DCRUST E-Summit '26. Teams were assigned a consumer soap brand and given 45 minutes to build a full campaign from scratch.
story.key_decision: Divided the 45-minute window across four concrete deliverables—a promotional poster, a short filmed ad, a live skit, and a product pitch for the stage round.
story.result: Finished 3rd Position Podium overall and won the ₹1,100 cash prize.

competitions.title: Venture Varsity (Field Pivot Run)
competitions.field_context: Collegiate startup elimination sprint. Eliminated in Round 1 on deck evaluation.

service_breakdown.name: Live on-campus service pivot
service_breakdown.mechanism: Direct customer acquisition on campus lawn after R1 deck elimination

deliverables: Direct customer acquisition on campus lawns

story.setup: Entered Venture Varsity at Ashoka University and suffered an early Round 1 deck elimination on theoretical metrics.
story.key_decision: Rather than packing up after elimination, walked out to the campus lawn with ₹0 and set up on a park bench to test real-world willingness to pay under a 2-hour window.
story.result: Generated ₹1,500 in 2 hours through rapid live service execution. The elimination and immediate field pivot proved that real customer transactions teach faster than deck slides.
story.takeaway: Rejection is field data. When a deck fails, test demand directly on the pavement.

competitions.title: Business Pitching — Iris Camera
deliverables: Carry Less. Create More. tagline & campaign brief

story.setup: Competed at DCRUST E-Summit '26 in the collegiate Business Pitching track.
story.key_decision: Engineered the 'Iris Camera' concept under the tagline 'Carry Less. Create More.' in a 3-member team with Tripti Kaushik and Raj Khatri.
story.result: Delivered the collaborative product presentation to the judging panel in the competition rounds.
story.takeaway: Rapid hardware concept positioning requires instant clarity of core user value.

competitions.title: Turn the Court (Impromptu Debate)
competitions.field_context: Collegiate dynamic impromptu debate where speakers must switch argumentation sides when judges clap.
deliverables: Dynamic position reversal on judges' clap

story.setup: Entered the Turn the Court impromptu debate at DCRUST E-Summit '26 with teammates Tripti Kaushik and Raj Khatri.
story.key_decision: Developed real-time adaptive framing to instantly pivot argumentative stance whenever the judges triggered side-swapping by clapping.
story.result: Competed through rapid rounds demonstrating cognitive flexibility and verbal agility under strict time pressure.
story.takeaway: Mastering conviction on either side of an issue is the fastest way to understand core trade-offs.

ventures.name: Tathya (तथ्य)
ventures.status_detail: Early research · eval set in progress
ventures.thesis: Research into how LLMs fail on non-standard Indian dialects (Punjabi, Haryanvi, Bhojpuri), and a verification layer to catch those failures.
ventures.problem: LLMs perform poorly on regional dialects due to token fragmentation.
features: Custom evaluation benchmark for Haryanvi, Punjabi, and Bhojpuri
Verification layer for government schemes and regional queries

lines.text: Research phase · building Haryanvi / Punjabi / Bhojpuri eval set

ventures.name: Krama (क्रम)

ventures.problem: Mandatory attendance cutoffs (75%) trigger sudden academic disqualifications without proactive recovery visibility.
features: Safe leave buffer calculation and recovery calculus
Encrypted local SQLite storage with zero account creation required
